argument.text: At time r set g_j=u_t·u_{x_j}. Smoothness and compact support give continuous compactly supported derivatives, so they are integrable by M001. On each coordinate line integrate by parts with M007, taking v=1; the boundary values of g_j vanish, so the integral of ∂_j g_j on that line is zero. M003 applies to the product-integrable coordinate-permuted derivative, giving ∫∂_j g_j=0. Expanding the product derivative yields ∫u_{x_j}·∂_j u_t=−∫u_t·u_{x_jx_j}. Summing over j and differentiating the finite Frobenius energy sum gives ∫e_t=2∫u_t·(u_{tt}−Δ_xu). N002 identifies E′ with ∫e_t, proving N003.

hypothesis_checks: ℝ is a normed additive commutative group.
Lebesgue measure is finite on compact sets.
∂_j g_j is continuous and compactly supported.
ℝⁿ is the measurable topological space.
Euclidean factors are measurable and their Lebesgue measures are S-finite.
ℝ is a real normed space.
The integrand is continuous compactly supported, so M001 gives product integrability.
